class.name: Intent
class.brief_description: Describes a request to start an Activity.
class.description:
Inspired by Android's Intent, trimmed to game UI needs. An Intent carries an [member action] (resolved to a registered Activity scene), optional [member data] / [member extras], and a set of launch [member flags].
[b]Flags[/b] control how [ActivityManager] handles the Activity stack: - [code]FLAG_SINGLE_TOP[/code] (1): reuse top Activity if it has the same action - [code]FLAG_CLEAR_TOP[/code] (2): clear activities above the matching one, then reuse it - [code]FLAG_NO_HISTORY[/code] (4): don't keep the new Activity in the back stack - [code]FLAG_REORDER_TO_FRONT[/code] (8): bring existing Activity to the top without destroying - [code]FLAG_NEW_CLEAR[/code] (16): clear the entire stack before starting - [code]FLAG_LOAD_SYNC[/code] (32): force the synchronous load path (skip async ResourceLoader thread + per-frame poll). Use this for tiny scenes where the extra frame of latency matters more than smoothness, or for tests that need a deterministic, immediate result.
Flags can be combined with bitwise OR: [code]intent.set_flag(Intent.FLAG_SINGLE_TOP); intent.set_flag(Intent.FLAG_NO_HISTORY)[/code].

method.name: get_action
method.description: Returns the action string registered with [method ActivityManager.register_activity].

method.name: get_extras
method.description: Returns the extras Dictionary. Use this for passing arbitrary parameters between Activities (e.g. [code]{"id": 42, "from": "main"}[/code]).

method.name: has_flag
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the given flag is set. Pass a [code]Flag[/code] enum constant.

method.name: set_flag
method.description: Enables a flag. Pass a [code]Flag[/code] enum constant, e.g. [code]intent.set_flag(Intent.FLAG_SINGLE_TOP)[/code].

members.member: The action string, matched against registered Activity scenes.
A Dictionary of extra parameters passed to the target Activity. Available in [method Activity._on_create] via [code]get_intent().extras[/code].

constants.constant: Reuse the top Activity if it has the same action — calls [method Activity._on_new_intent].
Pop everything above the matching Activity, then reuse it.
The new Activity is not kept in the back stack; it is destroyed when navigated away from.
If the Activity exists in the stack, bring it to the top without destroying anything else.
Clear the entire back stack and all dialogs before starting this Activity.

Force the synchronous load path: [ActivityManager] calls [code]ResourceLoader.load(...)[/code] directly and attaches the Activity within the same call instead of returning a [code]LOADING[/code] [ActivityProxy] that flips to [code]READY[/code] on a later frame. Useful for tests and tiny scenes. Web / single-threaded platforms always behave like this regardless of the flag.
